A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same V2X-R dataset, cooperative fusion pipeline, and MDD module. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, supplementary material, and references support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original V2X-R detection benchmarks, simulated-weather experiments, K-Radar evaluations, and MDD ablations, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V5 retains original detection and ablation results and additionally reports communication-cost calculations and localization-error experiments in supplementary Tables 10–11.

M1.justification: The four-stage fusion pipeline, SA2MA/SM2MM adaptations, radar-conditioned MDD, Algorithm 1, and training losses are retained. The corrected description of the best diffusion setting as T=3 matches the implementation and results already documented in v3 Tables 8 and 14; it does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: V5 adds evaluation with perturbed agent localization, introducing an input-condition scenario beyond the existing weather tests. V2X-R, K-Radar, the VoD qualitative comparison, detection tasks, and weather coverage otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: MACP is removed from the LiDAR benchmark comparison in Table 2 and its accompanying discussion, although its training-settings row and reference remain. Other main benchmark comparators are retained. Removing the all-dash LiDAR-only L4DR row from Table 5 does not remove an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New supplementary tests specify localization-error standard deviations from 0 to 0.6 m with validation AP@0.5, and communication volume and calculated latency using 4-byte elements and 27 Mbps transmission. Existing dataset splits, evaluation regions, weather-training procedures, and tabulated training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: V5 adds two substantive analyses of cooperative deployment: communication volume and latency across modalities and models in Table 10, and localization-error sensitivity across four models in Table 11. These extend the analysis beyond weather robustness and MDD design choices. Existing component and diffusion-depth/loss-weight ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests for its experiments. The standard deviations in v5's localization analysis specify injected perturbation strength, not uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: V5 substantially revises V2X-R results in Tables 2–4 and parts of Table 5. For example, test mAP at IoU=0.7 changes from 46.2 to 52.01 for radar-only CoAlign in Table 3 and from 84.60 to 82.44 for fusion AttFuse in Table 4. Communication and localization results are added. K-Radar and MDD ablation numbers are retained, while the best-depth description is corrected from T=2 to T=3.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the Gaussian reparameterization argument, denoising formulation, and loss-weight expression are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: the first simulated V2X dataset incorporating 4D radar, a cooperative LiDAR–radar fusion pipeline, and weather-robust MDD. The headline fog/snow improvements of 5.73%/6.70% are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 qualifies fusion superiority as applying to 'almost all' models and newly emphasizes variation in fusion benefits across architectures. The appendix adds an interpretation of sparse radar transmission and acceptable fusion overhead. The MACP-specific explanation is removed; existing K-Radar class-dependent limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3's supplementary Table 10 prints sequence identifiers, split membership, agent configurations, and towns. V5 replaces this disclosure with a reference to data_protocol.yaml in Section 7.3. Sensor, benchmark-training, weather-simulation, and MDD parameter details are otherwise retained, as are the code-access links.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds three remote-sensing classification references: Sparse Focus Network, SS-MAE, and the work on mining redundant spectra for a spatial-spectral masked autoencoder. The claimed research gap remains unchanged. Consolidating duplicate DAIR-V2X references does not remove that cited work.

P1.justification: V5 makes localized prose revisions and adds acknowledgements. It reorganizes supplementary results under 'Additional Results Analysis' and consolidates benchmark, MDD, weather-simulation, and K-Radar settings under 'Training Detail.' Most prose and the main section structure remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with additional plotted models and explicit IoU labels; Figures 3–4 receive visual refinements. Table 3's caption is corrected to identify radar-based methods. The appendix removes the sequence-list table, adds communication and localization tables, and relocates retained tables while preserving the overall document format.

improvement.justification: V5 adds useful evidence about communication overhead and localization robustness in Tables 10–11 and corrects the best diffusion-depth description to agree with Table 8. These provide a limited net gain, tempered by removal of printed sequence metadata and MACP results. The broad benchmark-value revisions are unexplained, and numerical inconsistencies remain, so changed scores do not themselves establish better quality.
